name: Why is the equity risk premium so high?
posed_evidence: Prescott in a study published in 1985
statement: Why have stocks earned a premium of five to eight percent a year over government bonds, a gap that standard economic models cannot explain?
status_source: Wikipedia, Equity premium puzzle: "the unexplained reasons driving this disparity"

name: Why do national savings and investment rates correlate?
posed_evidence: first documented by Martin Feldstein and Charles Horioka in a 1980 paper
statement: Why are domestic saving and domestic investment so strongly correlated across countries when capital can move freely to the best return worldwide?
status_source: Wikipedia, Feldstein–Horioka puzzle: "first documented by Martin Feldstein and Charles Horioka in a 1980 paper"

name: Why does capital not flow from rich to poor countries?
posed_evidence: famously discussed in a paper by Robert Lucas in 1990
statement: Why does capital not flow from developed to developing countries, although poor countries have less capital per worker and so should offer higher returns?
status_source: Wikipedia, Lucas paradox: "capital does not flow from developed countries to developing countries"

name: Why does the high-interest currency appreciate?
statement: Why does a currency with a higher interest rate tend to appreciate, when uncovered interest parity predicts it should depreciate by the rate difference?
status_source: Wikipedia, Forward premium anomaly: "the domestic currency appreciates when domestic nominal interest rates exceed"

name: Why is consumption uncorrelated with the real exchange rate?
statement: Why is the correlation between relative consumption and the real exchange rate near zero or negative, when full international risk sharing predicts a positive one?
status_source: Wikipedia, Backus–Smith puzzle: "the correlation between consumption and real exchange rates is zero or negative"

name: Why do firms pay dividends?
statement: Why do corporations pay dividends and why do investors pay attention to them, when dividends are taxed more heavily than capital gains?
status_source: Wikipedia, Dividend puzzle: "why do corporations pay dividends"

name: Why is the credit rating market so concentrated?
statement: What explains the concentrated market structure of credit rating agencies, where a few firms rate most of the world's debt?
status_source: Wikipedia, Credit rating agency: "The reason for the concentrated market structure is disputed"

name: What is the definition of disease?
statement: Is there a definition of disease that fits both the physiological process behind it and the patient's suffering and loss of quality of life?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "There is no overarching, clear definition of what a disease is"

name: How can evidence-based medicine guide care of an individual?
statement: How can results from trials on large samples of patients be applied to the care of one individual patient in evidence-based medicine?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "how results obtained from large samples of patients can be applied"

name: What causes idiopathic diseases such as aggressive periodontitis?
statement: What causes diseases of unknown origin, such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or aggressive periodontitis, and can treatment be found before the cause is?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "the cause of aggressive periodontitis"

name: How do paracetamol, lithium and antidepressants work?
statement: By what mechanism do paracetamol, antidepressants and lithium relieve symptoms, even though their effects on certain biological processes are known?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "Other examples are paracetamol, antidepressants and lithium"
